items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I ain't seen the day, even the day that Benny Goodman could play like Buster Bailey.

ctx.x: MR. GREER: He played all the lead instruments. But you think he's sitting with the philharmonic orchestra? No, because he's soul. But he was capable. I ain't seen the day, even the day that Benny Goodman could play like Buster Bailey. Buster ate him up like a turkey dinner. And Jimmy Hamilton, Barney. So, they splice him, the King of Swing. They'd carry him down. He playing the same thing out of Fletcher's book, years ago. Fletcher saved him. But right away they're going to make him the white champion.

Oh, I know what I wanted to ask you. Did you have -- at that time, too, do you think that's one of the reasons, given those kinds of pressures, are you saying that's one of the reasons why the guys -- like you were talking earlier about how the guys always are involved with dignity and having their presentations be real exact, everything on the button, guys look good, clean-shaven, you know, have their music down, have all their music memorized and everything, that that was a way of making sure that --
